title: At least 14 charged in alleged $22.5 million California train cargo theft scheme
orig_title: At least 14 charged in alleged $22.5 million California train cargo theft scheme
summary: Federal prosecutors said at least 14 people have been charged over an alleged scheme that stole cargo worth $22.5 million from freight trains in Southern California. Prosecutors say the crew hit at least 36 freight trains between February 2024 and August 2026, cutting air hoses to force them to stop. Prosecutors identified Nathan Daniel Angel, 21, of East Los Angeles, as the alleged leader, operating with his father and two uncles. Officials said a Los Angeles-based sneaker resale business, which was not an authorized Nike reseller, bought stolen sneakers and generated more than $1 million for the crew. The defendants are presumed innocent, and the maximum penalties include five years for conspiracy and 10 years for each theft count.

title: TxDOT Has A Simple Warning For Truckers After Lubbock's I-27 Bridge Accident
orig_title: TxDOT Has A Simple Warning For Truckers After Lubbock's I-27 Bridge Accident
summary: The Department of Transportation (TxDOT) has spoken out about truck drivers striking overpasses in Texas. The column recalls an October semi crash into the I-27 overpass in Lubbock, where the driver misjudged the height, and cites a Houston bridge that has been hit 16 times since January 2025. TxDOT also identified 61 instances of unreported bridge damage so far in 2026. The writer lists improperly measured vehicle height, misunderstood clearance postings and ignored warning signs as common causes, and notes that oversized trucks need permits because some roads and bridges are not designed for them. The writer advises drivers to know their vehicle's height and take another route if a bridge looks like a close fit.

title: Scottsbluff County Highway 71 Crash Kills Two Truck Drivers
orig_title: Scottsbluff County Highway 71 Crash Kills Two Truck Drivers
summary:
Two semi drivers died after their trucks collided head-on on Highway 71, north of Lake Minatare Road, outside Scottsbluff, on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, at about 9:10 a.m., according to authorities. The northbound driver was identified as 66-year-old Wesley Barkell of Pine Bluffs, Wyoming, and the southbound driver as 38-year-old Robert Henderson of Hemingford, Nebraska. The crash happened in foggy conditions. Three other vehicles drove into the scene and were damaged by debris before emergency crews arrived, but their occupants were uninjured.

Highway 71 was shut down in the area for about nine hours. The Nebraska State Patrol is conducting a full crash reconstruction, including post-crash inspections of both commercial vehicles, and no cause for the collision has been released.

orig_title: Three supply chain trends carriers should watch heading into 2027
summary: In a FleetOwner column, the chief executive of a Lincoln, Nebraska freight brokerage outlines three supply chain trends he expects fleet owners to watch in 2027. He cites Bureau of Labor Statistics data showing that trucking has lost more than 100,000 jobs since 2023, although the decline slowed in 2026. Using mileage and fuel-economy figures from the American Transportation Research Institute and Department of Energy diesel prices from early 2026 onward, he estimates that higher diesel costs add roughly $40,000 a year per truck, or $400,000 for a 10-truck fleet. He warns that if a recession pushed rates below operating costs, some carriers would be forced to haul freight at a loss. He also argues that driver shortages will keep pressure on pay, which fuel costs make harder to fund.

summary: Einride, the Swedish autonomous and electric freight company listed on Nasdaq as ENRD, said its contracted annual recurring revenue was about $167 million as of November 2026, up 76% from $95 million at the end of June. In a third-quarter business update issued November 18, 2026, it reported constant currency revenue of SEK 185.9 million ($18.3 million), a 27% rise from the second quarter. The company said it has added eight customers since June, bringing its total to more than 40. Its two cab-less electric trucks for EASE Logistics went into daily freight operations in Marysville, Ohio, in September. The company reaffirmed second-half 2026 revenue guidance of $39-42 million, but its adjusted EBITDA outlook for that period was widened to negative $39 to 41 million.

title: ATRI: Trucking’s annual congestion costs reach $128.2B
orig_title: ATRI: Trucking’s annual congestion costs reach $128.2B
summary: The American Transportation Research Institute (ATRI) estimates that highway congestion added $128.2 billion in trucking costs in 2024, according to its latest Cost of Congestion study. That was $4.7 billion more than in 2022 but slightly below the 2023 record of $129.8 billion, which the study linked to a prolonged freight recession that reduced truck mileage. ATRI counted 1.24 billion hours of delay in 2024, with an average congestion cost of $7,973 per truck. Texas, California and Florida had the highest state costs, and the top ten states accounted for 53% of the national total. New York City led metro areas at $7.49 billion, followed by Miami and Chicago. ATRI also estimated that 6.66 billion gallons of diesel were wasted in 2024, adding $25.04 billion in fuel costs.

title: FMCSA seeks input on using cameras in place of truck mirrors
orig_title: FMCSA seeks input on using cameras in place of truck mirrors
summary: FMCSA has opened a public comment period on a request to let fleets use Safety Vision's View Smart cameras instead of the two side mirrors required on commercial trucks and buses. A notice published Nov. 18 in the Federal Register says Safety Vision is seeking a five-year exemption from the rule requiring a rear-vision mirror on each side, and the agency has not approved the request. The system uses weatherproof cameras on both sides that feed video to screens mounted along the windshield, which the company says offers a wider view, better low-light visibility and alerts for nearby pedestrians or vehicles. Safety Vision has supplied the system to transit bus operators since 2024, though those buses still carry their required mirrors. FMCSA will weigh the application, safety analyses and public comments before deciding whether the system offers safety equal to conventional mirrors. Comments are accepted at Regulations.gov through Dec. 18 under docket FMCSA-2026-3707.

summary:
Connecticut State Police are investigating a fatal crash in Tolland that involved a semi truck's brake rotor. Troopers responded to a reported incident on westbound I-84 near Exit 69 around 12:45 p.m. on November 18. Investigators said Juan Marty Del Toro was driving a 2014 Nissan NV200 west when a 2019 Kenworth truck operated by Manpreet Singh was eastbound nearby.

Police said the Kenworth suffered a brake failure that caused rotors to come apart and become airborne. One rotor hit the Nissan, came through the windshield and struck Marty Del Toro, who was pronounced dead at the scene. A passenger was taken to a hospital for evaluation. Police asked anyone with additional information or dash cam video to come forward.

title: Commercial Driver's License: Saia LTL Freight; Application for Exemption
orig_title: Commercial Driver's License: Saia LTL Freight; Application for Exemption
summary:
The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration is asking for public comment on an exemption application from Saia LTL Freight, a company headquartered in John Creek, Georgia. Saia wants commercial learner's permit holders in its driver training program to operate combination vehicles with double trailers while under the direct supervision of a CDL holder with a doubles/triples endorsement. The notice states that it does not indicate what decision FMCSA will ultimately reach.

Saia has requested a 5-year exemption from two rules, 49 CFR 383.93(b)(1) and 383.37(a). According to the filing, approximately 300 trainees a year would use a fleet of about 19 training vehicles. Comments are due December 18, 2026, under docket FMCSA-2026-2642. After reviewing the application, safety analyses and public comments, FMCSA will either grant or deny the request.

title: Q3 2026 Cargo Theft Falls as Losses Rise
orig_title: Q3 2026 Cargo Theft Falls as Losses Rise
summary:
Verisk CargoNet reported 547 supply chain crime incidents involving cargo across the U.S. and Canada in the third quarter of 2026, down 33% from a year earlier and 19% from the second quarter. Estimated losses still rose 12% to $230.1 million. Fictitious pickups, in which criminals use deception to obtain a shipment, fell only 6% to 138, so their share of reported activity rose to about 25%.

Through September, reported incidents were down 25% year to date, while estimated losses rose 39% to $718.9 million. The average value of stolen goods with a documented value rose 72% to $448,456. CargoNet logged 19 thefts of $1 million or more, compared with nine a year earlier. California accounted for about a third of incidents, and four states made up 57% of the quarterly total. CargoNet also documented fraud schemes in 2026 that used compromised email accounts, internet phone systems and transportation applications, and said theft has historically risen in Q4.

ACT Research said freight demand improved for a third straight month in October and now believes the freight cycle has entered its growth phase. The Cass Freight Index shipments component rose 5.9% year over year in October, up from 1.9% in September, helped by an easy comparison with late-2025 trade war effects. Seasonally adjusted, shipments gained 1.7% month over month.

Expenditures on freight grew 27% year over year to 4.01 in October, from a 20% gain in September, driven by higher shipments, rates and fuel surcharges. The Cass Truckload Linehaul Index reached 156.2, up 0.9% month over month and 9.9% year over year, as both spot and contract rates rose. The source says the near-term direction seems higher still, and that normal seasonality would put November shipments up 3% year over year. Elevated inflation, rising interest rates and the temporary nature of IEEPA tariff refunds are cited as limits on demand.

Guilford Technical Community College in Greensboro runs a truck driver training program that staff say has grown every year since it started six years ago. The certificate takes eight weeks of full-time study or 14 weeks of nights and weekends, and costs about $1,800 including books. Jan Knox, VP of the college advancement foundation, said graduates can often find work right away at a salary of $60,000 or more.

Old Dominion Freight Line, a trucking company headquartered in the Triad, is funding four $1,000 scholarships a year at the college, two of them for women. Chris Brooks, Senior VP of HR at the company, said the awards help people who might not otherwise afford a CDL or a diesel mechanic certification. The company said it has over 200 women drivers.

title: Higher diesel prices strain farm transportation budgets
orig_title: Higher diesel prices strain farm transportation budgets
summary:
Higher diesel prices are adding costs for Iowa farmers and trucking operators, according to Matt Wells, vice president of the Mid-West Truckers Association. Wells cited refinery shutdowns, declining fuel reserves and the war between Russia and Ukraine as factors tightening supply. He said two California refineries were shut down and a refinery in Joliet, Illinois, was offline for seven to ten days, while Ukrainian attacks damaged Russian refining facilities.

Wells said transportation rates and operating budgets will need to reflect the higher costs, potentially for the next year to year and a half, and he does not expect diesel prices to fall significantly soon. He also cautioned that fuel prices do not always return to earlier levels after a large increase. On red-dyed diesel, Wells said the modern dyed product is essentially the same fuel as clear highway diesel, and that its use on public roads remains subject to federal and state tax requirements and any specifically authorized exemptions.
snippet: Higher diesel prices strain farm transportation budgets Iowa Agribusiness Radio Network

Fleet technology provider Samsara has opened its Agent Studio platform to all of its customers, letting trucking companies and other fleet operators build custom AI assistants. A voice feature can call a driver when the truck enters a geofence around a distribution center and give site-specific instructions. summary:
A federal appeals court in the Second Circuit on November 13 set aside a $73.5 million federal funding penalty against New York over nondomiciled commercial driver's licenses. The court found that federal officials were trying to enforce a licensing requirement that the governing regulations did not contain. Parriva asks whether California can use the same reasoning to challenge its own penalty.

An October 1 Federal Highway Administration notice shows $31,229,953 withheld from California, covering the period October 1 through December 11, 2026. California's separate dispute involves an estimated $158.3 million in fiscal 2027 highway funding, which does not mean that full amount has been withheld. The California case is docketed as No. 26-1027 before the D.C. Circuit and was scheduled for oral argument on September 11, 2026. Parriva said it could not verify a final merits decision as of November 14.

title: Field to Freight: John Deere Connects Farm Production With Renewable Diesel Alternatives
orig_title: Field to Freight: John Deere Connects Farm Production With Renewable Diesel Alternatives
summary:
John Deere is testing 100% biodiesel (B100) in five semi-trucks for six months under its Field to Freight initiative, according to an RFD-TV interview with John Deere Biofuels Director Nate Green. The trucks deliver parts and equipment to dealers and farmers from the company's distribution center in Milan, Illinois, and were fitted with an upgrade kit installed by Optimus Technologies. Penske, CPC Logistics and Chevron are also involved, with Chevron supplying the biodiesel.

The trucks use a dual-tank system to start on diesel and switch to B100 once the engine warms, and they recirculate diesel at shutdown. Green said the demonstration will show whether the technology works within the company's logistics network, and John Deere would consider wider deployment if it does. He also said full life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions from biodiesel can be 50% to 85% lower than petroleum diesel, depending on feedstock.

orig_title: U.S. rail carload and intermodal volume continues strong momentum in October, reports AAR
summary: The Association of American Railroads said U.S. rail carload and intermodal volumes stayed strong in October, according to its latest Rail Industry Overview. The AAR said 15 of its 20 tracked carload commodity groups rose from a year earlier, and 16 were up on a year-to-date basis. Grain, petroleum and petroleum products, chemicals and metallic ores led the year-to-date gains. The report called October intermodal volume "especially strong," citing the first, third and fifth-best intermodal weeks on record, and said 2026 is expected to set a new record. Cited drivers included high diesel prices, trucker insurance and maintenance costs, fewer available truck drivers and solid rail performance.

title: Two men sentenced after CBSA officers stopped an illegal crossing in Manitoba
orig_title: Two men sentenced after CBSA officers stopped an illegal crossing in Manitoba
summary: Two people have been sentenced over an illegal border crossing at the Sprague crossing in Manitoba. The Canada Border Services Agency said it stopped a minivan on May 7 because of "inconsistencies" in the driver's declaration, and officers found a 46-year-old man hiding in the trunk. That man, Temitope Omofuyi Davies, told officers he had paid the driver $1,000 to get him into Canada, and the agency later learned he had also been caught trying to cross near Surrey, B.C., in March. Davies pleaded guilty to failure to report on Aug. 19 and was sentenced to time served. The driver, Annan Nigel Ferguson, a 50-year-old American citizen, was sentenced on Nov. 4 to one year in prison for aiding and abetting failure to report. With time served counted, he has roughly three months left on the sentence.

summary: Bain & Company's 2026 new US Truck Study found that close to 80% of American fleet operators intend to make large equipment investments within six to 12 months. The survey of 210 operators also found that 79% expect fleet growth over the next 12 months, and more than a third of those expect growth of 10% or more. Bain linked the rise in demand to autonomy becoming a central focus and to Tesla expanding its capacity. For truck makers, the report's main point is having units ready to sell, saying availability wins. summary: A wrongful death lawsuit has been filed against Contract Transportation Systems Co. (CTS) and one of its truck drivers over a fatal crash on White Horse Road in Greenville, South Carolina. The complaint was filed Nov. 4 in federal court, on behalf of the estate of Leonard Harding McPeak Jr. The suit alleges that the CTS driver, heading northbound, pulled into a median turn lane and backed the tractor-trailer across southbound lanes while trying to reach a Sherwin-Williams store, so McPeak's pickup struck the trailer on Jan. 7. The plaintiff says McPeak suffered severe injuries and died, and accuses the driver of negligence and of violating South Carolina traffic laws and federal motor carrier safety rules. The suit also accuses CTS of negligent hiring, retention, training and supervision, seeks actual, consequential and punitive damages, and has requested a jury trial.

summary: FleetOwner's annual Trucking By the Numbers feature looks at driver figures for for-hire and private fleets. Citing the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, it puts the number of heavy- and tractor-trailer truck drivers at about 2.2 million in 2025. According to the American Transportation Research Institute, the ratio of drivers to trucks dropped to 0.9 that year, and for-hire annual turnover was about 44.2%, down from 48% in 2024. The article says turnover was highest at the largest truckload fleets, at 70.7%. A National Private Truck Council survey of 89 private fleet respondents reported a 17.1% turnover rate, with about 58% of private fleet drivers able to go home every night. Compared with the ATA annualized salary, the surveyed private fleets paid about 19% higher wages.

Robinson acquired DeSpir on June 22, 2026, and said the deal expanded its network of vetted, security-focused contract carriers. Saratoga Springs residents and city officials are again pushing to move tractor-trailer traffic off Van Dam Street. The push followed a late-night crash between a Skidmore College bus and a tractor-trailer that blocked traffic for hours at Van Dam and Clinton streets, though no major injuries occurred.

A five-ton weight limit ordinance the City Council passed in December 2023 came down within days, because the state said city officials had no authority to pass local ordinances on the state-designated route. A city request for a traffic study outlined rerouting trucks via Route 9 from Northway exit 14 in Malta or via Route 50 through Ballston Spa. The state said de-designating a route requires documented operational deficiencies or a provable history of accidents. A neighborhood association study counted upward of 700 trucks a day, and the Trucking Association of New York warned that de-designation could push trucks onto other routes.

title: Verisk CargoNet reports higher cargo theft losses despite fewer incidents
orig_title: Verisk CargoNet reports higher cargo theft losses despite fewer incidents
summary: Verisk CargoNet logged 547 cargo and supply chain crime incidents in the U.S. and Canada between July and September 2026, a 33% drop from the same period of 2025. Estimated losses still rose 12% to $230.1 million, up from $205.1 million a year earlier. The average value of stolen commodities with documented values climbed about 72%, to $448,456. Year-to-date losses reached $718.9 million, a 39% increase. Fictitious pickups numbered 138, close to the 147 recorded a year earlier, but made up about 25% of reported activity, compared with 18% in the third quarter of 2025. California reported 182 incidents, ahead of New Jersey with 46, Illinois with 40 and Texas with 43. Food and beverage was the top commodity category at 94 incidents, and metals ranked second with 63, including 34 copper thefts.
why: Fewer reported thefts do not necessarily mean lower financial risk for fleets, according to the article.
